ratio/batch: Sampling answers is slow, so we would like to make several updates from each batch of samples.
ratio/old: Call the model that sampled the batch pi old. After the first update, the model being trained, pi, already differs from it.
ratio/rho: So each sampled token is weighed by the ratio of its new probability to its old one, written with the Greek letter rho. Before any update, it is one.
ratio/eg: If pi old gave a token zero point two and pi now gives it zero point three, the ratio is one point five.
ratio/obj: The objective is the ratio times the advantage. Raising it makes tokens with a positive advantage more likely, and those with a negative one less likely.
clip/trust: But the samples only tell us about answers near pi old. Push a ratio far from one, and the estimate stops being trustworthy.
clip/clip: So PPO picks a small clip range, written with the Greek letter epsilon, often zero point two, and clips the ratio to between one minus epsilon and one plus epsilon.
clip/min: Then it takes the smaller of the clipped and the unclipped term.
clip/pos: With a positive advantage, the objective rises with the ratio until one point two, then goes flat: no reward for pushing further.
clip/neg: With a negative advantage, it rises as the ratio falls, until zero point eight, and then goes flat.
clip/wrong: Taking the smaller term means clipping only ever removes a reward. A ratio that moved the wrong way is still pulled back.
clip/why: So one batch can serve several updates, and none of them moves the model far. The KL penalty has a different job: keeping the whole run near the reference.
